messages:
sam: thinking out loud — can we add a lightweight "rollforward" helper to the deploy bot? not a full rollback, just a safe way to advance traffic away from a stuck canary and back to previous stable when things are flaky
leo: curious, how is that different from current /promote or /rollback commands?
sam: two differences: 1) automatic validation checks (error rate, latency) before shifting, 2) a single-step command to move traffic off a problematic canary to the last known-good without touching DB migrations etc
olga: example CLI idea?
sam: yep, prototype:

```
/deploy rollforward --canary-id=canary-2026-04-05 --to=stable --check=5m --metrics=err_rate,latency --grace=30s
```

should run quick health probes, wait grace period, then shift traffic 100% to stable. fall back to manual if checks fail.
leo: I like the single-command bit. We should also add an opt-in dry-run that prints planned steps and estimated token/ops costs for Redwood Dedicated customers
maya: small UX ask — add a short template for the release note entry so PMs know we did a rollforward, e.g. "rolled forward canary-xyz to stable due to elevated 95p latency"
release-bot: ack. can add a notifier that posts to #incidents and pings @oncall if rollforward runs during change window
devops-bot: suggestion: embed guardrails in the command, e.g. require --reason or --ticket for audit, auto-create audit record: `rfw-<ts>-<user>`
sam: agree. audit is must for private deployments too (KMS/HSM customers will want traceability). also proposal: add JS/Python snippets for infra-as-code to call the bot API programmatically.

```
// node example
await api.post('/deploy/rollforward', { canaryId: 'canary-2026-04-05', to: 'stable', checks: ['err_rate'] })
```

```
# bash wrapper
rgfw() { curl -X POST "$DEPLOY_BOT/api/rollforward" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d "$@"; }
```

olga: timers/ops question — should the command support staged percentages? e.g. 50 -> 75 -> 100 with health checks between steps
leo: yes, add `--stages=50,75,100 --wait=60s` to allow gradual rollforward. helps when traffic shapes are spiky
maya: and add a release-note template parameter `--note-template=rollforward-minor` so it auto-populates the console entry
sam: operational checklist to include in the template repo:

```
- verify canary logs
- run smoke evals against sample prompts
- check per-route latency 95p
- run /deploy rollforward --dry-run
- run actual rollforward with audit ticket
- post update to #releases and #oncall
```

leo: who wants to own a quick PR to the deploy-bot with the API endpoint and dry-run first?
olga: I can do the initial handler + stages logic, will ping devops for auth/audit hooks
maya: I'll add the release-note templates and a short console banner copy
sam: cool. can we aim for a small RFC in this channel by EOW and a canary test next week? tiny PoC is fine. :+1:
release-bot: created issue RFW-42: "deploy-bot: rollforward endpoint + dry-run + audit" assigned to olga; status: triaged
devops-bot: FYI added a checklist item to the oncall playbook: "if rollforward used, tag run id in incident ticket"
leo: nice — thumbs up. one more: add metric tag `rollforward=true` to any metrics emitted during the process so we can filter in console
sam: good call. ok folks — I'll draft the RFC and link the sample scripts in the issue. thanks!
